actions.oldValue: Freakonomics Radio (Apr 18, 2025), on lead producer Hal Luftig: "as Luftig told us, it made back only around 60 percent of its $11 million capitalization." https://freakonomics.com/podcast/on-broadway-nobody-knows-nothing/
actions.newValue: Industry contact (private, Nov 2026): the Broadway production went on to recoup and become profitable after closing, from royalties paid by the tours and international productions. At closing it had returned around 60% of its $11M capitalization (Freakonomics Radio, Apr 18, 2025, quoting lead producer Hal Luftig: https://freakonomics.com/podcast/on-broadway-nobody-knows-nothing/).

actions.oldValue: Commercial musical at the Palace Theatre (opened Apr 29, 2007; closed Oct 19, 2008 after 595 performances). Lead producer Hal Luftig says the Broadway run returned around 60% of its $11M capitalization (his 2006 pre-production budget was $12.8M, including a San Francisco tryout). It cost about $650K a week to run and grossed about $56M. Luftig says the several-year US tour recouped and made a profit, the London production made a small profit and the UK tour that followed was very profitable, and the show is licensed to hundreds of productions a year. Those productions pay royalties to the Broadway company, but no source yet reports the Broadway investors being paid back in full. A '75% by closing' figure that circulates online traces only to a January 2008 forum projection.
actions.newValue: Commercial musical at the Palace Theatre (opened Apr 29, 2007; closed Oct 19, 2008 after 595 performances). Lead producer Hal Luftig says the Broadway run returned around 60% of its $11M capitalization by closing (his 2006 pre-production budget was $12.8M, including a San Francisco tryout). It cost about $650K a week to run and grossed about $56M. It recouped after closing from royalties paid by later productions: Luftig says the several-year US tour recouped and made a profit, the London production made a small profit and the UK tour that followed was very profitable, and the show is licensed to hundreds of productions a year. No public report gives the date or the size of the eventual profit; 2012 is our estimate of when it crossed, after the US tour closed and while the London production ran.
